requirements.title: Preserve Server and storage architecture

Home Server remains default Execution Host; Source Location, execution environment, client connection and Project Move remain distinct. Cross-project operations are typed and permissioned, not arbitrary cross-vault database writes.

requirements.title: Preserve full platform execution
requirements.requirement: Native Windows/macOS/Linux and standalone Server products retain full execution capability; TrueNAS Apps and Unraid Community Applications wrap the canonical Docker Hub image; Kubernetes is a deployment/runtime target, not a different product database. Preserve TrueNAS modular Compose include and Unraid XML obligations; verify supported release at implementation time rather than freeze an obsolete current-version claim. WSL2 remains optional in Windows native and standalone products with no degraded health when off. Keep Apple Linux container execution and truthful native/virtualized/compatibility/cross-target proof. Provider-specific platform gaps do not reduce native Windows product support.

requirements.title: Preserve independent Project settings and continuity

No pervasive inherited/effective override UI. Keep Project templates versus configuration duplicates versus history duplicates distinct; logical layouts follow Project, physical window realization remains device/display-local. Client switching must not stop Goals/chats; background work survives GUI closure. Execution handoff and Project Move still use safe checkpoints, source reconciliation, fencing and explicit readiness before shutdown.

requirements.title: Preserve application update experience

Keep app, content/catalog and external-tool/source-control updates distinct. The Go connector updates with the PM release/image, not a new vendor updater. Daily/weekly/monthly backup retention must not resurrect a schedule picker in application updates.

requirements.title: Preserve safety and resource owners

Per-named provider CLI acquisition remains adjudicated; installation/setup/auth remain explicit, no project-triggered provider install. No offline-tool product. requirements.title: Scope changes are specific, not implicit

It deliberately expands default new Project backups to PM data plus source and Git/JJ history. Existing users are not silently opted into larger cloud uploads: migrate scope with review/acknowledgment. Restic with bounded rclone transports is the reference design, not permission to replace an already-proven equivalent live engine without evidence. Material new billing, external exposure, destructive deletion or extra secret export needs explicit user/admin consent.
requirements.acceptance: Publish an explicit migration/supersession record for these changes and preserve all unrelated newer live requirements.

requirements.title: Orthogonal identities
requirements.requirement: Represent local VCS (git, jj_git, or none), layout (colocated/non-colocated/shared workspace), Source Location, checkout/workspace, remote transport, forge and automation service separately. A RepositoryBinding carries stable project_id/repository_id/source_location_id/checkout_id/home_server_id/execution_host_id/environment_id; a RemoteBinding carries remote_id, fetch URL, one or more explicitly configured push URLs and credential attachments. ForgeBinding carries instance ID/product/version/tenant-account/resource repository ID. AutomationBinding may point to a different service from the Git host. Cursor Origin the product, lowercase origin remote name, and PM Server/Execution Host are three different concepts.
requirements.acceptance: Fixtures cover JJ+Forgejo, Git+GitHub, Origin-mirrored-GitHub with GitHub CI, multi-remote fork, SSH-only Git and non-Git. No keying on display path/name alone.

requirements.title: Effective operation capabilities
requirements.requirement: For each operation compute product support × adapter implementation × instance/version/tier/feature configuration × credential scopes × repository/branch permissions × PM policy × current locks/revision × connectivity. Persist support/evidence/freshness separately from availability. Expose ready, not_configured, auth_required, permission_denied, policy_blocked, protected, unsupported, adapter_missing, external_only, temporarily_unavailable, stale and unknown as distinct states with remediation. Unknown is not unsupported; unavailable checks are not zero failed checks; cached permission never authorizes a mutation.
requirements.acceptance: The same capability decision feeds GUI availability, command palette, NL/agents, Doctor and dispatch; backend rechecks at execution. Invalid/stale capability revision yields typed recoverable failure.

requirements.title: Remote targeting and authority
requirements.requirement: Each publish/fetch/review operation resolves an explicit repository, remote, forge instance/account and revision. Preserve distinct fetch and push URLs. An Origin mirror retains GitHub write authority and known PR mapping; never send the same push to Origin and its mirrored GitHub destination automatically. User-configured push fan-out requires per-target preview, idempotent tracking and partial outcome receipts: multiple remotes are not an atomic transaction. Forks and mirrors sharing commits are not automatically the same repository identity.
requirements.acceptance: A changed active project/account while a request is pending cannot retarget it; partial fan-out reports exactly which refs reached which target.

requirements.title: Git and JJ operation semantics
requirements.requirement: Git mode owns staged/unstaged/index/HEAD distinctions, commit, stash, branch/upstream and Git worktrees. JJ mode owns current @ working change, change IDs versus commit IDs, describe/new/edit/split/squash/abandon, bookmarks/tracking, conflicts, workspaces and operation history. Do not show a fake Git staging area or implement JJ save as hidden git commit/stash. Colocated Git/JJ share storage; coordinate locks and imports/exports to avoid double mutations. Changing chosen VCS is a migration/adoption operation with preview, not a theme/provider dropdown side effect.
requirements.acceptance: Git/JJ paired fixtures verify commands and labels differ, graph selection remains stable, operation-log undo is distinct from source commit history and backup restore.

requirements.title: Normalized data without semantic loss
requirements.requirement: Common models include ReviewRequest, ReviewThread, Check, AutomationDefinition, AutomationRun, JobOrStage, LogSegment and RemoteArtifact, with provider_kind, instance/account/repository, raw_status, normalized_status, immutable external ID, revision/SHA/change version, canonical URL and observed_at. Retain vendor extensions instead of flattening away approval policies, child pipelines, environments or manual gates. Identity includes service instance: PR #12 is not globally unique. Normalized display may say Reviews, but object detail uses Pull request or Merge request as the provider does.
requirements.acceptance: Roundtrip projection fixtures preserve native states/IDs and cannot mislabel GitLab MR as GitHub PR or Azure stage as fabricated GitHub step.

requirements.title: Operation reconciliation and external side effects
requirements.requirement: For pushes/merges/reviews/CI dispatch/cancel/rerun, record intended target and preconditions before external call; include idempotency where provider supports it, otherwise reconcile by exact remote object/commit/run/correlation evidence after timeout. Do not blindly repeat a non-idempotent merge, comment or dispatch. Show outcome_unknown while checking. Force operations require a current expected head/lease and explicit dangerous-action policy. A successful CLI exit is not proof the desired remote state exists.
requirements.acceptance: Timeout-after-success does not create duplicate PRs/runs/comments; revoked scope or branch change invalidates pending approval; tests distinguish accepted request from observed durable outcome.

requirements.title: Freshness, events and subscription ownership
requirements.requirement: One Home Server capability and observation service owns webhooks/polling/cache for each authorized binding, not one poller per UI client. Webhooks are optional authenticated accelerators with replay/ordering checks; poll reconciliation remains available. Never enable Funnel/public ingress merely to receive a webhook. Cache keys include all instance/account/repository/revision IDs; stale results from prior selection are discarded. Bound pagination, log streams, retry jitter, 429 backoff and inactive subscriptions via shared governors.
requirements.acceptance: Many clients and undocked panels do not duplicate underlying work; webhook delivery twice, cache staleness and repository switch races produce correct projections.

requirements.title: Local and remote responsibility
requirements.requirement: Git/JJ filesystem operations run on the Source Location's authorized execution environment, through selected installations and Worktree/Workspace Manager plus FileSafe. Hosting APIs may execute on the Home Server or authorized egress host, but cannot assume that its filesystem holds the checkout or that its credential is interchangeable with Git/SSH login. A CLI hosting adapter such as Origin is bound to a proven installation/profile and explicit -R target. Results return to the Home Server's durable project receipts; no worker becomes Project authority.
requirements.acceptance: A TrueNAS Home Server with WSL checkout and remote Forgejo instance routes each phase correctly with environment, credential and source lineage.

requirements.title: Assisted automation consumes same capability graph
requirements.requirement: Goal/planning agents, review helpers and CI monitors receive compact typed available-action summaries and blockers; they invoke the same registered commands. No whole forge registry/log dump in prompts. Automated publish/merge/CI actions require exact task policy and approval, cannot bypass protected branches, and must disclose CI/cost triggers. A forge runner is not a PM Execution Host unless explicitly configured; PM must not silently register its execution pool as an Actions/Pipelines runner.
requirements.acceptance: A requested unavailable action routes to supported alternative or structured blocker, never fabricated success, UI scraping as hidden substitute, or another provider account.

requirements.title: Cursor Origin read and write
requirements.requirement: Treat Cursor Origin as a Git hosting service with clone/fetch/pull/push subject to authentication, branch protection and PM policy. Its GitHub mirror mode changes authority and routing, not a provider-wide read-only flag. Correct any current prose, capability fixtures, disabled controls or agent rules that infer no push from destination preparation instructions. Preserve all ordinary permissions: read/write support does not mean permission to push every branch. Do not assert the previous integration agent made a particular mistake without inspecting its diff/report; record the old ambiguity and the actual live correction found.
requirements.acceptance: Origin standalone and mirrored fixtures have explicit read/write capability decisions; a missing PR API does not disable Git push; protected branches still reject mutations.

requirements.title: Origin hosting actions and CLI boundaries
requirements.requirement: Use the documented Origin CLI through an Integration Adapter where a stable public API is not established. Support documented PR list/view/create/diff/checks, editing, ready/draft, review/comment, review-thread reply/resolve/reopen, merge/close/reopen and stale-version refresh. Use JSON output and explicit repository/head/base/target; do not depend on current working branch defaults. Separate source checkout/forced checkout from read-only PR view. A create --push flag must not bypass publication preview/approval. Pin/test actual CLI output and auth interfaces; do not reuse Cursor Agent authentication as proof of Origin access.
requirements.acceptance: Recorded golden adapter outputs cover reads/writes/errors; PR create never unexpectedly publishes; revision-specific review and merge stale-head guards are tested.

requirements.title: Origin mirror, checks and platform disclosure
requirements.requirement: For an Origin mirror show GitHub-authoritative repository and mapped PR provenance. Bind workflows/actions/issues to the actual service that owns them; code mirroring does not duplicate CI secrets/settings/history. Keep .github workflow files as ordinary Git tree contents. Origin checks can be shown without inventing an Origin-hosted CI engine. Native Windows currently needs a verified supported Origin installation path: official WSL instructions are not proof of native Windows CLI. Offer explicit WSL or remote compatible host setup when needed; other native Windows capabilities remain healthy. Never install/enable WSL implicitly.
requirements.acceptance: Origin mirror+GitHub CI shows one correlated review/check set, no duplicate dispatch; WSL-off native Windows shows a narrow Origin-tool capability explanation, not global PM degradation.

requirements.title: Forgejo and Gitea first-class integration
requirements.requirement: Add distinct Forgejo and Gitea product/instance adapters using common HTTP/auth/pagination/error/cache primitives. Support custom instance URLs, API roots/base paths, SSH URL/port, private CA selection, known-host fingerprints, multiple accounts and organizations. Probe version and supported API schemas with bounded safe reads. Target repository list/create/connect/fork where supported; PR lifecycle, diff, reviews/comments, checks/status, releases/artifacts and branch policy as separate capabilities. Do not declare Forgejo forever API-identical to Gitea, or disable ordinary Git when the web API is turned off.
requirements.acceptance: Per-product fixtures include old/new instance version, disabled API, read-only token, enterprise CA, SSH-only transport and multiple instances with identical repo names.

requirements.title: Forgejo and Gitea Actions

Implement supported operations through that product's API, not rewritten GitHub endpoint guesses. Preserve provider-specific workflow syntax, secrets, variables, runner labels and permission behavior. Editing a workflow file is local source control; enabling a repository feature, registering a runner or storing a secret is a distinct privileged remote action. An unavailable runner is different from no workflow and no permission.
requirements.acceptance: Run list can be supported while dispatch remains unavailable; legacy instances use explicit external-only links where API capability is unimplemented, with no fake workflow rows.

requirements.title: GitHub and GitLab
requirements.requirement: Preserve full existing GitHub operational features and direct API ownership; gh is not a hidden requirement. Distinguish github.com from enterprise instances and their API/version/SSO policy. GitLab integration uses Merge requests and Pipelines, supports provider-specific approval/mergeability, stages/jobs/traces/artifacts/manual actions/child pipelines only when available. Do not translate every GitHub operation into a guessed GitLab equivalent. Keep action-specific service permissions, fork security, source/target branches and SHA identity. New generic dispatch commands may delegate to existing GitHub handlers; they do not erase provider-specific contracts.
requirements.acceptance: Regression inventory maps every current GitHub panel section/action to retained behavior; GitLab fixtures preserve MR naming and job/stage data with accurate unknown/permission states.

requirements.title: Azure DevOps Services and Server
requirements.requirement: Separate Azure Repos Git, Azure Pipelines and organization/project/account identity. Services authentication uses supported Microsoft Entra flows; do not build new integration on legacy Azure DevOps OAuth. Azure DevOps Server/on-premises has separate version/auth/endpoint capability profiles. Show Repos PRs, branch policies and Pipelines stages/jobs/steps/approvals/artifacts as supported, not GitHub names. TFVC is not covered by Git/JJ support: detect and explain it without pretending to open a Git checkout. Pipeline execution and deployment approvals need independent privileges.
requirements.acceptance: Services/Server and Git/TFVC fixtures select the right capabilities; org/project changes invalidate pending commands; no legacy OAuth/app registration demanded.

requirements.title: Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center
requirements.requirement: Use separate Cloud and Data Center instance/auth/version profiles. Cloud supports Bitbucket PR and Pipelines capabilities through documented APIs. Data Center must not inherit Cloud Pipelines automatically; expose proven external CI integrations and commit build status with provenance. New Cloud onboarding uses supported OAuth or scoped API tokens, not deprecated app passwords. REST and Git credentials are adapter-specific, not a universal username/password template. Preserve workspace/project/repository identifiers, approvals/tasks/merge checks and branch restrictions where supported.
requirements.acceptance: Cloud and Data Center fixtures differ in pipeline availability, authentication and URLs; older credential records migrate through reauthentication prompts without exposing values.

requirements.title: Generic Git, local-only and multi-forge repositories
requirements.requirement: A generic Git remote or SSH bare repository supports proven transport without a forge API; JJ is a local VCS layer and never offered as a cloud hosting account. Local-only/non-Git projects retain applicable Files, backups, tests and tools without fake PR/CI panels or forced GitHub setup. Support fork/upstream, more than one hosting provider, fetch via mirror and push to canonical host. Provide an explicit hosting/automation selector only where ambiguity exists; defaults derive from saved binding, never string origin alone. Preserve user pin/hide preference even when temporarily unsupported.
requirements.acceptance: Matrix includes no remote, generic SSH Git, JJ+Origin and a GitHub fork with GitLab upstream; selection never cross-publishes or silently changes default remote.

requirements.title: One Source Control panel and one automation panel
requirements.requirement: Keep source_control as the local/source-and-review operational panel. Generalize the existing github_actions occupant into a single provider-neutral Actions & Pipelines occupant (candidate canonical ID repository_automation; reuse an equivalent newer live ID if present). Migrate old github_actions serialized panel IDs, routes, order, hidden/More state, keyboard slot, width and undocked state through aliases into the same occupant. Preserve all GitHub Actions functionality. No per-forge icon, second rail, merged Git-only icon or backup/Server panel. The shell switch command remains view-only, not a repo fetch or remote mutation.
requirements.acceptance: Migration fixture opens an old saved GitHub Actions layout with the same position/order/size and no duplicate occupant; GitHub-only user loses no action or keyboard behavior.

requirements.title: Source Control header and section census
requirements.requirement: Header identifies repository/workspace and compact local engine plus hosting label, not six infrastructure identities. Details expose Home Server, execution environment, source path, remote fetch/push targets, authentication and observed revision. Required section census: changes and diff; staging/commit or JJ working change; branch/bookmark tracking; remotes/publication; history and graph; conflicts; stashes where valid; worktrees/workspaces; review requests and changed files/comments/checks; recovery/operation history; source protection/backup link. Inventory every additional section in the live current panel and retain or explicitly migrate it; this list is a minimum, not permission to drop unlisted sections.
requirements.acceptance: Live pre/post section inventory records each control, state, command and disposition; tests use Git, JJ and no-forge profiles at narrow/default/wide widths.

requirements.title: Git and JJ visual behavior
requirements.requirement: Git changes group Staged and Unstaged with index-aware diffs and Commit. JJ shows Current Change, description, parent/change context, New Change/Edit/Split/Squash and bookmarks; staging/stash controls are hidden as semantically inapplicable, with history/operations discoverable. JJ graph preserves both stable change ID and current commit ID, rewritten/abandoned/conflicted state, local/remote bookmarks and current @. Operation History displays operation time/description and safe inspect/restore preview. A backup snapshot is labeled separately from a JJ operation. No UI-only mapping from Stage to JJ squash or from Commit to arbitrary snapshot.
requirements.acceptance: Same file-selection gestures produce correct engine-specific commands; never present JJ edits as unstaged Git or send raw Git mutation behind a JJ action.

requirements.title: Reviews and publication details
requirements.requirement: Use common Review list shell with provider vocabulary (PR or MR), native status, source/target refs, author, draft, permissions, review threads, checks and currentness. Show actual push destination in Publish preview including Origin mirror write-through; separate publish from create review unless one explicit combined preview lists both effects. Offer branch/bookmark selection and expected-head guard. Display remote read/write/protection limitations with reasons. Surface unknown/outcome pending distinctly from failed. No blanket read-only Origin badge.
requirements.acceptance: Fixtures cover protected branch, rejected push, mirror PR mapping, stale review head, one-to-many push partial success and a review API unavailable while push remains ready.

requirements.title: Actions and Pipelines section model
requirements.requirement: Panel header selects automation binding only when multiple services apply. Sections: current revision checks; pinned definitions; available workflow/pipeline definitions; active and recent runs; queued/scheduled/manual gates; run details; native stage/job/step hierarchy where supported; streamed logs; artifacts/retention; environments/deployments/approvals where supported; runner and secret/variable settings deep links. Keep provider brand and native names in headings/details (GitHub Actions, GitLab Pipelines, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines, Forgejo/Gitea Actions). Generic Git has no fabricated definitions; Origin can show Checks from GitHub/other connected CI, not a fictional Origin Actions engine.
requirements.acceptance: Section matrix machine/panel_sections.json is applied to all provider profiles; a missing step API shows a job trace, not invented steps; existing pinned GitHub workflows and rerun controls survive.

requirements.title: Hide, disable and show external action correctly
requirements.requirement: Hide sections genuinely inapplicable to the selected local engine/service, but preserve saved layout and explain availability in capabilities/details. Disabled actions remain discoverable when setup/permission/policy/retry can fix them, with a specific reason and owner deep link. External-only actions explicitly say Open in <service>; they do not appear to complete in PM. Failed discovery yields Could not check capabilities, not empty success. Do not automatically reorder rail icons or jump focus during capability refresh; pending actions capture original context.
requirements.acceptance: Transition fixtures cover supported→auth expired→restored, service disabled, no runner, API unsupported, unknown and stale; keyboard focus stays predictable.

requirements.title: Related Files, Artifacts, Testing and status surfaces
requirements.requirement: Files adds engine-correct decorations/ignore behavior, repository/source badges only where useful, read-only backup preview route and Restore this file deep link. Artifacts distinguishes provider CI artifacts from PM runtime outputs and backup exports, retaining provider expiry/checksums/provenance and explicit import/download. Testing/Run Debug can link checks and reproduction receipts but do not equate remote CI success with local test proof. Assistant Chat consumes compact capability and action receipts, no extra forge/host banner. Bottom bar shows publication/backup/connector work truthfully without routine Synced or secret content. No backup statistics become model token usage.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-panel deep links preserve exact repo/revision/artifact/backup IDs and Client-vs-Server destination; provider artifacts cannot auto-execute after download.

requirements.title: Visual, interaction and performance proof
requirements.requirement: Use selected finalized concept source pipeline, not direct generated-HTML surgery. Preserve all eight themes, SVG-only iconography, no emojis/decorative left-edge bars, supported Slint target, reduced motion, contrast, focus, touch and keyboard behavior. Capability rows and logs paginate/virtualize; inactive/undocked observers do not duplicate backend work. Show phase-based ObservableWork progress, never fake fixed percentages. Demonstrate dialogs, submenus, transitions, narrow panel clipping, account/repo switching and errors through deterministic fixtures. Auth and recovery-key flows use non-secret fixtures and prohibit capture of actual secrets.
requirements.acceptance: Build/render every affected state/theme and watch meaningful animations where tooling exists; report not-run visual checks honestly instead of a screenshot inventory claiming motion proof.

requirements.title: Minimum provider profiles
requirements.requirement: Maintain separate profiles for github_cloud, github_enterprise, gitlab_saas, gitlab_self_managed, azure_devops_services, azure_devops_server, bitbucket_cloud, bitbucket_data_center, forgejo, gitea, cursor_origin_native, cursor_origin_github_mirror and generic_git. Local VCS matrix is separate: git, jj_git_colocated, jj_git_noncolocated and none. Matrix dimensions include Git transport, repository discovery/create, PR/MR read/write/review/merge, checks, workflow/pipeline definitions, run/log/artifact read, dispatch/cancel/rerun, webhook/poll, branch policy, secrets/variables, runner management and external URL fallback.
requirements.acceptance: Every profile has explicit capability status/probe/reason; no boolean “GitHub-compatible” passes all dimensions.

requirements.title: Repository identity and self-hosted trust
requirements.requirement: Validate provider instance base URL, tenant/account and API path before credentials are attached. Permit approved self-hosted subpaths and custom SSH ports even though PM public web hosting uses a dedicated-hostname baseline. Private CA trust is a scoped trust record; never global disable-TLS. Redirects and pagination links cannot leak Authorization to another origin. SSH fingerprints require first-use owner review or verified known-host entry; DNS/repository name alone is not proof. Metadata endpoints and localhost are blocked unless explicitly authorized for that host/network use.
requirements.acceptance: SSRF, redirect-to-other-host, custom basepath, enterprise CA, changed host key and same-name different-instance fixtures all produce correct trust gates.

requirements.title: Scoped forge authentication
requirements.requirement: GitHub uses PM-direct supported OAuth/App/token profiles with enterprise/SSO readiness and Git credential-helper attachment separately. GitLab uses per-instance registered OAuth/PKCE or scoped PAT; Azure Services uses Entra and Server its supported instance auth; Bitbucket Cloud uses OAuth/current API tokens and Data Center versioned supported tokens. Forgejo/Gitea default to a guided scoped PAT when no instance OAuth app exists, or use registered OAuth/PKCE when configured. Origin uses supported official CLI browser auth/credential helper on the owning environment. Do not ask for account passwords or silently grant admin scopes for ordinary clone/push/review.
requirements.acceptance: Profile matrix identifies issuer, allowed host, setup method, token ownership, scopes, refresh/revoke and Git-vs-API roles for every provider.

requirements.title: Administration is optional and risk-tiered
requirements.requirement: A service exposing repository-delete, force-push, policy editing, runner registration, secret write or organization management does not make it an ordinary one-click action. Preserve permission tier, preview, confirmation and currentness. CI secret values are write-only or reference-only where provider forbids readback; Settings never offers Reveal based on an API that cannot return them. API absence and insufficient token scope produce distinct explanations. Do not test sign-in by triggering a CI job or modifying branch policy.
requirements.acceptance: Admin capabilities are individually gated, destructive tests use synthetic fixtures/sandbox only, secrets are absent from results/logs.

requirements.title: Server-owned authentication state
requirements.requirement: Persist AuthSession metadata with session ID, initiating Client, owning Server/host/environment, provider instance, connection/profile, requested method/scopes, return route/object context, expiry, nonce/PKCE references and status. Keep tokens/verifiers/code values in a secret channel/store, not ordinary seglog events. Opening official sign-in happens on the active Client's system browser. Refresh/close/reconnect resumes the same session; timeout and cancel revoke the pending session safely. A localhost redirect on the laptop is not the container's localhost.
requirements.acceptance: Native, web-only, SSH and container flows complete on the exact original row/profile; replayed/mismatched callback fails closed with no token in audit output.

requirements.title: Native, device and web callback admission
requirements.requirement: Use only methods the named provider and registered app actually support: authorization code with PKCE, allowed device authorization, official paste-code/CLI flow or scoped token entry. Native callback bridge accepts one validated auth transaction and forwards its result to the owning Server over authenticated PM transport. Web-only headless flows use a registered provider-supported web callback/secure broker or approved device flow—not fabricated Google OOB/device support or an unregistered arbitrary custom domain. Human AuthBrowser is last supported fallback, isolated/unrecorded and never a bypass of provider embedded-browser restrictions.
requirements.acceptance: Callback ownership and registered redirect are verified per method; unsupported combinations show precise setup alternatives, not blanket use embedded browser.

requirements.title: Scope selection, reconnect and credential use
requirements.requirement: Connection UI shows service, account, instance and requested permissions in readable terms. Ask for extra scopes only when the requested operation requires them. Persist refreshable profile state in the owning Server/environment vault or external secret reference, survive container replacement, and serialize refresh writes per profile. Sign Out detaches/revokes only that connection/profile with dependency preview; no global deletion of user CLI profiles. Copy Project settings reuses an authorized binding, not a token copy. General build/test processes never inherit all forge/cloud/provider credentials.
requirements.acceptance: Expired token, concurrent refresh, signout with other Projects, external profile and redeployed container tests demonstrate correct isolation.

requirements.title: Source mutation and API orchestration
requirements.requirement: Repository edits route through local Git/JJ and Worktree Manager, hosting changes through ForgeAdapter, CI changes through AutomationAdapter. A composite publish-and-review operation has explicit ordered suboperations and receipts, not untracked shell chaining. Directory/branch/path revision locks use shared governor leases. Named-Plan, Goal, thread, source-location, environment, account and initiating Client lineage is attached where present without becoming authority. Output/network errors are scrubbed before events/Usage/Chat.
requirements.acceptance: One GUI action, palette invocation and automation request traverse the same semantic handler; no duplicated private panel implementation or silent cross-host fallback.

requirements.title: Separate backup products and default scope
requirements.requirement: Retain internal recovery snapshots, settings copy/transfer, Project Backup and Full Server Backup as separate products. New normal Project Backup scope is PM Project data + Project files + Git/Jujutsu history. Advanced PM-data-only and selected-source scopes clearly disclose exclusions. Do not re-enable source uploads for existing plans without review. Full Server Backup includes catalog/global non-secret settings, selected/all Vaults, required durable blobs, integration/profile metadata and placement maps; it is not an installer image or runtime process dump. Rebuildable indexes/caches/tool binaries/build outputs are excluded unless an explicit recovery requirement names them.
requirements.acceptance: Scope preview shows exact included/excluded families and repository coverage; old plans retain their previous scope until confirmed; PM-data-only can never claim full source/JJ recovery.

requirements.title: One coordinator, established encrypted engine
requirements.requirement: PM Backup Coordinator owns consistency, scope, retention intent, authority and restore semantics. Use a version-pinned BackupEngineAdapter; restic is the reference encrypted snapshot/dedup engine, with native object/SFTP/REST backends and bounded rclone transports for Drive/OneDrive/WebDAV where needed. Reconcile an already-integrated equivalent engine on the live repo by evidenced capability rather than installing a second owner. Do not design new cryptography, change canonical PM storage, wrap every backup in redundant rclone-crypt, or use rclone sync on live Project Vaults. Engine/transport binaries use existing governed tool lifecycle, pinned schema/format, SBOM/license/provenance/repair/rollback and platform checks.
requirements.acceptance: Owner map has one backup coordinator and engine contract; protocol/format versions and engine choice admission evidence are recorded; no bespoke unaudited crypto or live-file synchronization appears.

requirements.title: Independent recovery boundaries
requirements.requirement: Default to independently recoverable per-Project backup repositories/sets plus a separate Server catalog backup set, even when they share one bucket/account. Do not couple every Project to one mutable global dedup/pruning database. A Full Server Capture Manifest references exact Project snapshots by capture_set_id, engine repository_id, snapshot_id, schema version, consistency vector and source coverage. Deduplication within each repository is permitted. Shared credentials or RecoverySet do not merge authority, lock, retention or recovery boundaries. No new remote backup backend becomes canonical state.
requirements.acceptance: Corrupt/quarantine one Project backup repository without losing other Projects; full-server restore rejects incoherent arbitrary combinations of latest snapshots.

requirements.title: PM storage consistent snapshot
requirements.requirement: Acquire a documented backup barrier from each storage owner: close/flush the relevant seglog boundary, capture non-rebuildable canonical redb values using supported consistent snapshot/export semantics, record projection/replay watermarks, and freeze referenced CAS blob manifests. Do not copy open redb/seglog files opportunistically. Tantivy and derived redb projections may rebuild. Full Server capture establishes a catalog/Vault manifest consistency vector and detects Project create/remove/move races. Materialize an immutable staging generation or verified filesystem snapshot then release work before network upload.
requirements.acceptance: Crash/concurrent-write fixtures restore a valid Project at declared watermarks; capture pause does not last for the cloud upload; insufficient staging capacity produces bounded waiting/failure.

requirements.title: Distributed source capture and real consistency
requirements.requirement: Capture source on the authorized host/environment owning each checkout: server-local, mounted NAS, WSL, Apple Linux environment, container/Kubernetes volume or SSH remote. Preserve source_location_id and workspace maps, not literal foreign OS paths as universal truth. Use filesystem snapshots where available or controlled quiescence plus traversal/hash verification; PM locks alone do not stop external editors. Detect external mutation during copy, retry within budget or label the result non-atomic/partial; never certify it complete without evidence. Offline required source hosts cause Waiting for source or a clearly partial snapshot, retaining the prior complete backup.
requirements.acceptance: Backup during external editor writes, source host failure and remote mount disappearance cannot return full success; source transfer follows FileSafe containment.

requirements.title: Complete Jujutsu operation recovery
requirements.requirement: A source-inclusive JJ backup captures operation heads/store, referenced repository views, commits/trees/conflict state and underlying object storage required by retained operations, plus workspace metadata/current files. Include non-current/abandoned/rebased objects still needed for operation recovery, not merely current bookmarks. Discover actual repository/workspace layout, Git common directory, alternate/shared object stores and linked workspaces; bundle verified dependency closure or report explicit missing coverage. Suspend/coordinate JJ/Git GC/prune/rewrites during capture. Text jj op log, Git push, mirror clone or Git bundle alone are insufficient.
requirements.acceptance: Restore on a clean isolated host with original checkout unavailable; list operation history, inspect historical views and restore a chosen earlier operation with object verification. Test colocated, non-colocated and shared/multi-workspace layouts.

requirements.title: Git history, dirty files and dependency closure
requirements.requirement: Capture Git refs/object packs/required reflog state within declared retention and current dirty tracked files plus approved required untracked files. Include required LFS objects and submodule repositories/worktrees or explicitly mark unhydrated/missing content and recovery dependence; pointer files are not binary backup coverage. Follow external object directories only through explicit approved dependency maps; never crawl all of HOME, SSH keys or mounted hosts. Exclusions cannot remove .jj/.git metadata while still labeling history included. Previously garbage-collected history cannot be recreated by a new backup.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture covers Git common-dir/worktree .git pointer, LFS/submodule offline restore, dirty files and an excluded required object; partial coverage is visible and never counted complete.

requirements.title: Source secrets and exact history
requirements.requirement: Exclude PM credential stores, cloud tokens, CLI authentication profiles, raw SSH keys and tsnet identity from ordinary Project backups. Allow explicit separately encrypted portable-secret backup only under existing proven portability rules. A secret already committed in Git/JJ history is historical source content: exact history preservation and universal historical secret removal cannot both be promised. Provide detection warnings and optional separately classified redacted export, never silently rewrite historical backup. Ignore-file and secret-file scope decisions are visible and evidence-backed.
requirements.acceptance: Tests distinguish excluded PM secrets from a historical repository secret; a redacted export is not advertised as an exact recoverable JJ repository.

requirements.title: Upload and verification states
requirements.requirement: BackupRun phases: planned, waiting_for_source, waiting_for_unlock, acquiring_capture_barrier, capturing, staged, encrypting_uploading, committing_remote_snapshot, verifying_structure, verifying_data, completed or partial/failed/cancelled. Maintain independent capture completeness, per-destination upload state, integrity verification level and restore-test status. A committed remote snapshot is not a tested restore. Incomplete uploads are not selectable complete recovery points; cancellation leaves bounded cleanup-safe orphan data. Multi-destination failure never erases successful copies or collapses into all-green status.
requirements.acceptance: Interrupted upload, checksum failure, one-destination quota and successful upload without restore-test are represented truthfully; receipts list exact snapshot IDs and verification levels.

requirements.title: Portable and automatic without client lifetime
requirements.requirement: Backup plans, scheduler, writer lease, credentials and resumable outbox are Server-owned. Closing a browser/native client does not stop them. Project Move preflights backup credentials/destinations then explicitly transfers the one schedule/writer assignment or preserves designated source ownership with a clear policy; old and new Servers cannot independently prune the same repository. Updating PM can drain/checkpoint uploads and resume by durable generation, never rerun destructive maintenance blindly.
requirements.acceptance: Move/restart/client-loss scenarios have one writer/maintenance authority, no duplicate scheduled jobs and no credential copying through Project state.

requirements.title: Destination families and names
requirements.requirement: MVP destination targets: Amazon S3; other S3-compatible services/user-hosted object storage; Backblaze B2; Azure Blob Storage; Google Cloud Storage; Google Drive; Microsoft OneDrive; local/NAS/shared folder; SFTP; WebDAV/Nextcloud; compatible self-hosted backup REST endpoint. B2 is not consumer Backblaze Computer Backup; GCS is not Google Drive; Amazon S3 is one named provider, not a duplicate Amazon row. Each adapter declares list/read/write/commit/lock/delete/version/object-lock/archive/stream/resume support and credential needs. Do not hard-code universal S3 parity or immutability.
requirements.acceptance: machine/backup_destinations.json maps every named service/family to supported auth, engine/transport and limitations with explicit unsupported features.

requirements.title: Add destination GUI and safe validation
requirements.requirement: Flow: choose service → authenticate/select existing profile → choose bucket/container/drive/folder/prefix → choose region/endpoint only when required → safe test → review encryption/scope/schedule/cost notes → save. Reuse same Settings authentication controls and return context. Destination test writes/reads/deletes only a named random canary inside an explicit PM-owned scratch prefix after approval; read-only tests never mutate. Do not alter bucket ACL, enable public access, create billable resources or destroy an existing repository as a test. Detect existing backup repository and offer Use existing, never initialize over it.
requirements.acceptance: Canary identity/content/cleanup receipt scoped to selected prefix; path collision and read-only credential produce exact explanation without partial bucket reconfiguration.

requirements.title: S3, B2, Azure and GCS authentication
requirements.requirement: S3 supports user-scoped access keys/session tokens or supported runtime/workload credentials; B2 uses supported application keys and its S3-compatible endpoint by default. Azure Blob supports only methods verified for selected engine/transport (for example scoped SAS/account or Entra/workload adapter); GCS similarly uses proven ADC/service account/workload attachment where supported. Do not promise an engine accepts every cloud credential type. Store credentials by secret reference, rotate without rewriting backup data, refresh temporary credentials safely and expose bucket/prefix/region/account identity separately from secrets. Network endpoint/TLS trust validation prevents credential exfiltration to untrusted S3-compatible URLs.
requirements.acceptance: Provider-specific sign-in/readiness matrix tests expiry/rotation, least privilege, prefix restriction, external secrets and engine method compatibility.

requirements.title: Drive and OneDrive ordinary sign-in
requirements.requirement: Provide Connect with Google and Connect with Microsoft through supported production OAuth registrations owned/configured by PM, not rclone's retiring shared client and not an end-user developer-console tutorial. Use supported official pages, PKCE/state, return to exact destination, store refresh credentials on the backup-owning Server and persist across container replacement. Request narrow file/folder access where compatible with operation and account type. For Drive prefer verified drive.file app-created/selected backup objects; existing-backup discovery after reinstall must be tested. For OneDrive evaluate Graph app-folder scopes separately for personal/business/tenant availability; do not claim preview/limited scopes work universally. Override broad rclone defaults explicitly.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh login, enterprise consent denial, account swap, business/personal drive, existing-repository reauthorization and token refresh fixtures pass without global Drive access silently added.

requirements.title: Headless web OAuth is a release prerequisite
requirements.requirement: For native PM use approved installed-app redirect/callback forwarding. For browser-only Docker/TrueNAS/Unraid, require a provider-supported registered web callback or approved device flow for that provider/scope. Do not assume Google Drive has a generic headless device/OOB flow. Where necessary, provide a narrowly scoped PM-operated authorization callback/token-exchange broker under PM's registered OAuth app: no PM user account, no Project/backup/key storage, only short-lived auth exchange and encrypted delivery to the paired requesting Server. Bind provider state/nonce/PKCE and intended Server/Client; delete transient material. Confidential app credentials stay on the broker, never embedded in distributed binaries. User-managed registered apps remain Advanced. Provider approval/verification and maintained callback infrastructure are explicit release gates, not fake working client IDs.
requirements.acceptance: Web-only real-provider auth acceptance is blocked until registrations/redirects/consent/security evidence exist; plan integration may finish with these implementation prerequisites named, never claim runtime login tested.

requirements.title: Self-hosted transports and existing services
requirements.requirement: SFTP uses scoped SSH key/agent attachment, fingerprint verification and path bounds. WebDAV/Nextcloud uses supported OAuth/app password/token, TLS and scoped server path; do not infer support solely from a successful HTTP response. NAS path is local to owning Server, mounted with OS credentials outside Project content; missing/disconnected mount is not an empty new repository. Compatible REST servers require tested protocol/auth and optional append-only mode. Google/OneDrive synchronized desktop folders are filesystem destinations only if consistency/exclusive writer can be proven; prefer direct APIs for cloud backups.
requirements.acceptance: Disconnected mount, changed SSH key, redirected WebDAV origin, wrong REST protocol and partially synced folder produce safe errors without initializing a new backup set.

requirements.title: Credentials, connection errors and consent
requirements.requirement: Cloud destination credentials are distinct from forge accounts, model-provider accounts, backup decryption keys and tailnet enrollment. Reuse authorized existing credential references only within permitted scope. Automatic credential refresh is fine; scope expansion, account switching, new destination enablement and costly archive retrieval require human policy/consent. Cancellation/signout disconnects that destination without deleting backup data. Restored metadata with no credential shows Reconnect destination. Secrets go through dedicated protected submission channels and bounded helper process configuration, never command lines, history, URLs, telemetry or world-readable rclone files.
requirements.acceptance: Storage auth loss does not report lost decryption key; token/test errors are scrubbed; exporting normal settings reveals only profile references.

requirements.title: Cloud-drive and archive limitations
requirements.requirement: Display quota/full/throttled/unavailable/reauth/tenant-restricted distinctly, honor Retry-After and bounded resumable transfers, and avoid whole-drive scans. Cloud drives are mutable/deletable by the owner; do not advertise them as ransomware-immutable. Provider object versions/trash and PM snapshots are different histories. Cold storage requires supported restore/retrieval status, possible fees and availability delay; unsupported archive-tier repository layouts are blocked or marked external recovery required, not silently treated like hot S3 storage. A generic cloud lifecycle rule cannot expire live deduplicated packs by age.
requirements.acceptance: Quota, 429, user-deleted pack, cold-object retrieval and wrong folder identity tests preserve previous recovery points and truthfully explain recovery impact.

requirements.title: Encryption and confidentiality boundary
requirements.requirement: All cloud/remote backup payloads—including file names, PM manifests, chat/memory and source-control metadata—are encrypted/authenticated before leaving the trusted backup worker. Use the chosen engine's established format and key derivation; transport uses validated TLS/SSH as appropriate. Explain that provider-visible object sizes, timing, account/bucket identifiers and necessary format/key-slot metadata may remain visible. Server-side encryption alone is insufficient; PM does not keep a cloud escrow decryption copy. Bind repository identity and trusted manifest to reject wrong-destination restore; detect rollback where locally known freshness evidence exists, without promising detection after all trusted local state is lost.
requirements.acceptance: A remote object dump contains no source/chat/file-name plaintext; corrupted objects fail authentication; documented threat model distinguishes confidentiality, deletion and stale-snapshot rollback.

requirements.title: RecoverySet and engine keys
requirements.requirement: Generate a cryptographically random recovery credential with at least 256 bits entropy on the backup-owning Server using the platform CSPRNG; format it for human copy with a canonical encoding, never derive it from Project/account names. User label is Backup Recovery Key. A RecoverySet identifies the independent repositories it unlocks; a simple default may reuse this credential across that set while each repository retains its own engine-generated master keys and independent metadata/retention. State the scope plainly. Separate encryption domains use separate RecoverySets, not per-setting overrides. Use engine-supported password/key slots, not custom envelope/KDF algorithms.
requirements.acceptance: A recovery key successfully unlocks only its declared set; fake packet fixtures contain no real key; losing one Project repository cannot corrupt others despite shared recovery credential.

requirements.title: Secure key handoff in GUI
requirements.requirement: After repository initialization show a dedicated human-only recovery screen: Save Recovery Kit; Copy Recovery Key; optional system print view; explicit reminder that PM cannot recover it if all copies are lost. Kit contains format/engine version, RecoverySet and repository IDs, destination locator hints, key, and step-by-step restore instructions—not cloud login tokens or provider/tsnet secrets. Default kit is intentionally sensitive readable recovery material: clearly label it; user may store in password manager/encrypted storage. Do not silently upload it beside backups. Deliver via authenticated no-store secret response to the initiating Client; Save targets the Client's file picker/download, not the remote Server filesystem. No key in query strings, QR telemetry, clipboard history managed by PM, service-worker cache, browser storage, screenshots, agent context or normal logs.
requirements.acceptance: Remote web and native Client can save the kit locally, preview only after authorization, and never leak it into command receipts or trace fixtures; cancelled file save is not recorded as confirmed recovery.

requirements.title: Confirmation, later export and local protection
requirements.requirement: Offer Test Saved Recovery Kit: re-import/select the saved kit or enter key in a secret form and perform a read-only engine unlock/manifest test. This proves usability, not that a durable independent copy exists; keep separate user acknowledgment and verified unlock status. Skipping yields Recovery not confirmed and a bounded reminder, not false successful handoff. Later re-export requires owner step-up approval and an available protected key attachment. Unattended scheduler uses the Server secret store, OS key protection or administrator-supplied container/Kubernetes secret injection; if unavailable/locked, show Unlock required. Do not conceal a plaintext key in generic config to make unattended mode appear ready.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh process unlock, service restart, cancelled export, lost kit while local key survives and locked key-store scenarios have exact states; no ordinary agent can reveal/copy recovery credentials.

requirements.title: Loss and rotation are different operations
requirements.requirement: Cloud account access alone does not decrypt backups. If both user recovery credential and all protected local engine-unlock copies are gone, encrypted backup content is unrecoverable; state this clearly. Routine add/remove/change unlock credential uses engine key-slot APIs and verifies every repository in the RecoverySet before retiring a prior slot. It does not re-encrypt old data or neutralize an attacker who already copied keys/ciphertext. Suspected compromise requires a new encryption domain/repositories, verified re-encryption/copy of selected retained history and controlled retirement; previously exposed historical copies remain potentially exposed.
requirements.acceptance: GUI distinguishes Change recovery access from Re-encrypt after compromise; interrupted multi-repository rotation retains at least one working credential and clear per-repo state.

requirements.title: Key delivery command and authorization rules
requirements.requirement: Generic commands carry recovery_set_id and secure_submission_ref/export_session_ref, not raw recovery keys, OAuth codes or tokens in persisted payloads. Export sessions are short-lived, audience-bound, one-use where practical and marked no-store; stream secret to authorized human client only. Authorization is checked at creation and redemption; reconnect/client revocation invalidates it. Key presentation is separate from backup browse authority: permission to list snapshots need not permit decryption-key export. Clipboard auto-clear is best effort only and must not erase unrelated new clipboard content; explain OS clipboard persistence limits.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover expired/stolen export refs, revoked Client, concurrent viewers, logs and agent tools; sensitive response schema is absent from normal event/projection exports.

requirements.title: Recovery kit maintenance and identity exclusions
requirements.requirement: When repositories/destinations are added or relocated, preserve stable IDs and provide Updated Recovery Kit where locator/format/key scope changed. Existing kit should remain useful via repository discovery where possible; do not imply a stale locator is a lost encryption key. Keys/profiles/connector identity stay outside ordinary Project backups. Portable Full Server backup still excludes tsnet secret state by default; explicit disaster recovery inclusion requires separate approved secret section and protection against two active copies of a node identity. Restoring as new always creates/re-pairs independent Server/connector identity.
requirements.acceptance: Project copy/move/source-inclusive backup never includes tsnet state; Full Server restore-as-new cannot boot a cloned tailnet node.

requirements.title: Existing and fresh-install entry paths
requirements.requirement: Settings Data Backup and Retention → Restore opens current destinations and an Add existing backup option. A fresh native/standalone/container PM installation exposes Restore existing PM data after safe local Server claim/bootstrap and before optional provider/new-Project onboarding. It can import a Recovery Kit or accept destination+repository/key, connect storage, discover remote snapshots and rebuild a local backup catalog without the old Server catalog. Public unclaimed setup is never enabled as a recovery shortcut. Do not require model-provider authentication to restore backups.
requirements.acceptance: Destroy fixture local PM catalog and source machine, then recover from cloud destination and saved kit through native and web GUI only.

requirements.title: Locate, authenticate, unlock and inspect
requirements.requirement: Wizard: choose existing destination or import kit → validate locator/trust → sign in to storage → select existing repository → unlock with Recovery Key → load encrypted manifests → choose snapshot → inspect coverage and compatibility. A kit is untrusted input: validate schema/size and user-review new endpoint before sending credentials; key and destination account are separate. Never run restic init on an apparently empty/unreachable existing backup. Show missing credentials, wrong key, wrong repository, revoked access, corrupt metadata and unsupported future format as distinct recoverable errors.
requirements.acceptance: Malicious kit URL, wrong account/key and missing manifests cannot overwrite backups or exfiltrate credentials; browsing works without preexisting catalog IDs.

requirements.title: Snapshot browser and safe content preview
requirements.requirement: Provide search/filter by Project, capture date/time/timezone, snapshot ID, host/source, verification and scope. Snapshot details show PM data, files/history/JJ operation coverage, unavailable sources, retention/hold and restore-test result. File tree is paginated and read-only; text/diff/history previews are treated as untrusted content, not active workspace files. Never execute HTML/scripts/macros/hooks from a preview. Preview limits and redaction apply; content to agents requires separate user permission. Artifacts show sizes and provider retrieval conditions.
requirements.acceptance: Large snapshot trees remain responsive; malicious HTML and symlinks do not escape preview; selection is pinned to immutable snapshot ID not changing latest.

requirements.title: Retrieve and export without activation
requirements.requirement: Actions: Download selected file(s) to this Client; Extract to a chosen Server/Execution Host folder; Compare with current file/revision; Export a portable encrypted backup using engine-supported format/copy; browse only. State destination explicitly—This device versus named host—and inspect required data transfer permissions. Decrypted export carries a warning that saved files are no longer protected by backup encryption. Export preserves manifest/dependency closure when advertised as a full Project backup; a partial file export is not a restorable Full Server archive. No requirement for FUSE or an OS-mounted backup filesystem.
requirements.acceptance: Native and browser downloads use the selected Client, remote extraction uses explicit host/path, and cancellation removes bounded temporary output without deleting user files.

requirements.title: Restore modes and preview
requirements.requirement: Support Restore as New Project (safe normal default), Restore Project in place, selective PM data/source/file restore where dependency closure is valid, and Full Server replacement through maintenance/recovery mode. Preview shows snapshot IDs, source coverage, host/path mappings, current target revision, overwrite conflicts, required migrations, disk space, key/profile availability, permissions, retained/excluded secrets and suspended work. A selective restore must include dependent records/blobs or block invalid combinations; source code only is explicitly not PM data rollback.
requirements.acceptance: Mode fixtures cannot replace live Project merely by opening a snapshot; selective chat/Goal/artifact references remain valid or blocked with reason.

requirements.title: Safe apply, rollback and path remapping
requirements.requirement: Require owner confirmation/step-up for in-place/full replacement, create and verify pre-restore recovery unless a documented emergency consent accepts its impossibility, acquire target leases and stop conflicting mutations, stage and verify before activation, then atomically activate where supported. FileSafe applies to extraction/restoration including symlink/reparse traversal, case/Unicode collisions, reserved names, executable bits, UID/GID/ACL/xattrs, absolute path remaps and untrusted hooks/config. Cross-filesystem or remote activation without atomic rename needs an explicit journaled rollback contract, not a pretend atomic guarantee.
requirements.acceptance: Crash at every phase, target edit after preview, low space, Windows/Linux path collisions and remote failure either restore old state or expose a precise recoverable boundary.

requirements.title: JJ and Git verification after restore
requirements.requirement: Restore source into an isolated workspace/repository boundary and verify object closure, refs, operation heads/views, working-copy mappings, dirty files, selected historical JJ operation and required LFS/submodules. Use version-compatible native verification/read commands; avoid inadvertent snapshotting by read commands when supported ignore-working-copy mode is needed. Full JJ operation replay testing occurs on a disposable restored copy, never on the active original. Do not run source hooks, trust restored global Git config/credential helpers, push branches or resume Goals automatically. Reconnect missing credentials/tools explicitly.
requirements.acceptance: Lost-machine fixture proves an older operation can be inspected/restored without contacting the original forge; restore without LFS closure is marked incomplete.

requirements.title: Project and Server identity reconciliation
requirements.requirement: Restore-as-new assigns new PM Project identity and rewrites identity-sensitive internal references while preserving lineage; external forge repository identity stays external and is not renamed automatically. Same-Project in-place restore records a recovery epoch and revalidates outstanding execution leases/approvals. Full Server replacement accepts only consistent catalog/Vault capture sets; starts in recovery-safe mode with remote access, schedules and executions gated until identity/trust/profile readiness is verified. Default foreign-machine restore creates new Server/connector identity and pairs clients again. Exact identity takeover requires explicit fencing of original host, not merely observing it offline.
requirements.acceptance: Two restored Servers cannot concurrently use one project writer lease or tailnet node; old CI/push requests are not replayed; new Project retains provenance without duplicate live request IDs.

requirements.title: Retrieval cost, progress and durable completion
requirements.requirement: For archival storage show retrieval waiting/fees and request consent per policy before billable retrieval; generic adapters unable to stage archives must explain external restoration prerequisite. RestoreRun persists immutable selection, per-source/destination phases, retry state, validation and outcome receipts on the recovery coordinator, surviving Client disconnect. Full Server replacement progress has a recovery endpoint/reconnect token not stored only inside the catalog being replaced. Completion separately reports data restored, source verified, indexes rebuilt, auth missing and workloads paused. No automatic resume from recovered in-memory process fiction.
requirements.acceptance: Web refresh/full-server restart and cold retrieval remain observable; failure does not become success when UI reconnects; output evidence identifies precise recovery point.

requirements.title: Scheduling and user policy
requirements.requirement: Provide Automatic Backups On/Off, protected scope and one or more destinations. Recommended initial policy is a design default: daily scheduled capture with timezone-aware execution, keeping seven daily, four weekly and six monthly recovery points; it is editable and must not override existing chosen policy. Record timezone/DST, missed-run coalesced catch-up, permitted hours, minimum spacing and unique schedule occurrence IDs. Event-triggered recovery such as pre-update/pre-restore remains separately classified from daily offsite policy. Avoid one scheduled job per connected Client.
requirements.acceptance: DST repeat/skip, sleeping/offline host, duplicate event and multi-client fixtures produce at most one scheduled occurrence and truthful missed-backup state.

requirements.title: Bandwidth, costs and backpressure
requirements.requirement: Use RuntimeResourceGovernor for capture/CPU encryption/compression/hash/IO/network and process leases, preserving interactive/resume/approval reserve. Limit concurrent per-repository mutation, stage storage, upload concurrency/bandwidth, log size and retries. Optional metered-connection/time-window/cloud quota/cost alerts should stop or defer gracefully according to policy; no hard-coded current cloud prices. Foreground restore and background backup priorities remain explicit. Backup metrics are maintenance diagnostics, never API token usage.
requirements.acceptance: Backup+Goals+browser recording remains responsive under resource pressure; full staging queue and provider throttling cannot exhaust disk or block UI.

requirements.title: Retention, legal hold and pruning
requirements.requirement: Retention applies to snapshots by repository and scope; legal holds/pins and minimum protected recovery points override automatic expiry. Preview separately lists snapshots to forget, bytes eligible for prune and confidence; dedup estimates are not guaranteed exact savings. Use engine reachability-aware prune after verified mutation lease, never cloud delete-older-than-N on packs. Keep at least the last known good recovery point unless explicit high-risk delete-all consent. Project removal from this Server does not implicitly delete remote backups.
requirements.acceptance: Hold, concurrent upload, failed new snapshot, last-good retention and Project deletion tests preserve recoverability and prevent cross-Project destructive pruning.

requirements.title: Immutability and credentials
requirements.requirement: Encryption is not deletion/ransomware protection. Offer append-only/versioned/Object Lock protection only for a tested backend+engine+maintenance profile, explaining locks/retention/fees and any required privileged maintenance separation. Do not simply check an Object Lock box on a restic bucket: lock files, pack rewrites/prune and credential permissions may conflict. Routine backup credential should lack unnecessary destructive authority where backend permits; protected prune uses separate short-lived authorization. User-owned Drive/OneDrive remains deletable. Do not silently change retention compliance locks.
requirements.acceptance: Capability fixtures include unsupported object-lock mode, delete-denied ordinary writer and approved maintenance window; immutable promises require actual restore/deletion-resistance evidence.

requirements.title: Verification and restore drills
requirements.requirement: Track structural verification, full data-read verification, sampled verification and isolated restore drill as distinct levels with timestamps and exact coverage. Schedule bounded checks and optional periodic drills; disclose egress/time/storage costs. Latest upload verified structurally cannot inherit another snapshot's restore-tested badge. Corruption quarantines affected recovery points without deleting alternatives. Drill restores untrusted files without execution, validates PM consistency and JJ history, writes a receipt, then cleans its own staging area.
requirements.acceptance: Corrupt an old shared pack and prove all affected snapshots are identified where knowable; show untested history honestly; no dry-run test marked as actual full data read.

requirements.title: Crash, lock and history operations
requirements.requirement: Persist job intent and phase before side effects; reconcile partially completed engine operations after restart. Do not blindly remove repository locks because another process is temporarily unreachable; verify local owner/process or explicit recovery override against remote writer policy. Cancellation is phase-aware: capture may retry, upload can resume from engine semantics, activation/prune may need finish/recover rather than unsafe kill. Retain bounded encrypted-source provenance and human receipts, not secrets. Downloaded backup history/search cache is derived and rebuildable.
requirements.acceptance: Power-loss/expired lease/stale-lock fixtures show bounded recovery and no concurrent restore/prune; receipts remain available from other clients.

requirements.title: Normal manager and detail areas
requirements.requirement: Normal overview: Automatic Backups, Protected data (All/selected Projects; PM data + files + Git/JJ history), destination cards, Encryption enabled, Last complete remote backup, Recovery kit status, Back Up Now, Restore and Add Destination. Detail areas: History and Browse; Destinations; Schedule/Retention/Holds; Recovery and Keys; Advanced/Diagnostics. Preserve current storage/pressure/quarantine/cleanup/recovery manager sections rather than replacing them. Server/Project scope selectors are explicit; no hidden new inheritance system.
requirements.acceptance: Current manager section census includes retained storage lifecycle and new cloud workflows; simple healthy screen does not expose engine binaries, object keys or raw OAuth config.

requirements.title: Destination cards and authentication
requirements.requirement: One card per named destination shows service/account label, region or folder summary only where useful, Ready/Needs sign-in/Quota full/Waiting/Failed, last complete backup and one primary action. Expanded view exposes connection test, permissions, retention, bandwidth, encryption domain, verification, cost notes and logs. Account and decryption readiness are separate. Sign In opens official system-browser flow and returns to the row after refresh. Add destination never treats server file pickers as client paths or vice versa.
requirements.acceptance: Cards across cloud object stores, drives and self-hosted paths use the same reusable projections; wrong-account and key-locked states are independent.

requirements.title: Recovery screens and contextual links
requirements.requirement: Recovery Keys area supports status, Save/Copy/Test kit, rotation and compromise recovery with human-only step-up UI. History opens read-only snapshot details/tree and Restore mode chooser. Source Control/JJ Operation History can offer Back Up Project and Browse Backups links scoped to repository/Project without creating a second backup implementation. Files offers restore/download/compare historical selection; Projects offers backup and restore-as-new. Full Server restore is reachable from safe bootstrap and Settings but never a regular single-file context-menu action.
requirements.acceptance: Every link maps to existing backup-domain command with snapshot/project/host context and back-navigation preserved; no secret export reachable from agent/NL automation.

requirements.title: Onboarding and Doctor reuse
requirements.requirement: Installation/Deployment, Server Claim/Bootstrap, Product Onboarding and Doctor remain distinct owners. Bootstrap can restore existing data; product onboarding can connect a backup destination and confirm Recovery Kit after first Project; both invoke canonical commands. Doctor consumes projections for destination auth, path access, recent complete backup, source/JJ coverage, verification, retention/holds, pending cleanup, key-store unlock and recovery-kit confirmation. Missing optional destination or intentionally disabled WSL is not global degradation. Repairs route to owning commands, not new Doctor-only scripts.
requirements.acceptance: One failing optional path does not mark everything broken; Doctor and onboarding call the same protected flows/receipts as Settings.

requirements.title: Alerts, progress and safety copy
requirements.requirement: Use existing notification inbox/title-bar mechanisms for actionable backup failures and bounded reminders; no new toast center or rail panel. Bottom bar may show Backing up, Waiting for source, Restore in progress or Backup needs attention with compact popover, without crowding Update Available and Server route state. Say Last complete backup only for scope-complete committed copy; show verification separately. Explicit copy warns recovery key loss, plaintext export, cold retrieval costs, in-place replacement and exact source/JJ exclusions. Never display real keys in concept fixtures or recordings.
requirements.acceptance: Deterministic UI states cover long-running work, foreground/background switching, secret redaction, reduced-motion and screen-reader announcements.

requirements.title: Only Go helper, unchanged user architecture
requirements.requirement: Ship signed pm-tailnet-connector embedding tailscale.com/tsnet with the Rust Server over authenticated versioned local IPC. No full app, tailscaled/general CLI, MSI/EXE nested Tailscale installer, macOS system extension/VPN profile, TUN/NET_ADMIN networking requirement, official full Tailscale sidecar/operator, tailscale-rs, Tailcat or backend selector. Existing host Tailscale is user-managed and may coexist; PM only records verified external endpoint routes. Exact GUI label remains Tailscale / Built into PuppetMaster. This replaces previous whole-package bundling across native, standalone and container packaging.
requirements.acceptance: Source preservation map verifies all TSN-001..020 and detailed contracts; negative scan of active live canon and packaging finds no PM-owned full Tailscale dependency.

requirements.title: Userspace client egress and private web behavior
requirements.requirement: A tsnet node does not configure the OS/browser routing or DNS. Native PM connections to private tailnet servers therefore use a bounded connector Dial/stream IPC route, or a separately user-managed reachable host-tailnet endpoint, rather than assuming ordinary socket dial resolves MagicDNS. Only approved PM server endpoints are allowed; no open SOCKS proxy or arbitrary LAN pivot. One persistent node per PM Server installation can serve both ingress and authorized egress, not per Project/WSL/session. An ordinary web browser still needs private network reachability or Funnel/reverse proxy/Remote Link; embedding tsnet in PM does not magically enroll that browser.
requirements.acceptance: Native PM can reach private tailnet through helper without host VPN; browser-only private route displays accurate prerequisites; arbitrary outbound destination through helper is denied.

requirements.title: Listener lifecycle and ingress distinction
requirements.requirement: Validate pinned tsnet listener semantics before implementing private HTTPS and optional ListenFunnel on a port. Do not simultaneously bind incompatible private/Funnel listeners to the same address. Use supported combined listener with ingress-aware policy or distinct tested listeners; FunnelOnly excludes private traffic and is not the private default. Public enable/disable must preserve authorized private access and not expose setup/internal/debug/credential-helper endpoints. Ingress classification is derived from trusted connection metadata, never requester-controlled forwarded headers. Headscale remains private/custom-control tested and never receives a Funnel promise.
requirements.acceptance: Enable/disable/restart Funnel with live private clients, exact origin/auth/WebSocket tests and Headscale unsupported-public state; no listener port conflict or unauthenticated setup leak.

requirements.title: Backup and auth traffic are not tailnet identity
requirements.requirement: Cloud backups connect from their authorized owning Server to the user's storage endpoints and do not automatically travel through PM Remote Link/TURN/DERP or PM-operated storage. Forge/cloud account authorization and recovery keys are distinct from Tailscale node identity. The same PM secure UI transport can carry protected user input, but never stores it in connector logs/state. Project copy, Move, source snapshots and cloud Project backups exclude node secret state; portable Full Server backup default exclusion persists. Restore new Server re-pairs a new node; exact same-host internal rollback follows collision-safe identity recovery.
requirements.acceptance: No default cloud backup bill/load on PM relays, no node identity in source-inclusive snapshots, and no backup unlock through a tailnet login.

requirements.title: Packaging and versions stay release-owned
requirements.requirement: Docker/TrueNAS/Unraid run the PM helper in the canonical PM image; Kubernetes may use PM-owned helper process/sidecar with one-active persistent identity. Windows native/standalone do not depend on WSL to run this helper. Pin compatible Go/tsnet/IPC versions with PM releases; drain/reconnect and rollback do not discard keys. Underlying transport session interruption must not repeat a push/merge/backup/prune/restore command; continue using operation IDs/currentness reconciliation.
requirements.acceptance: Connector upgrade/restart during publication, backup upload and remote restore leaves one operation and authoritative receipt; packaged full Tailscale binaries absent.

requirements.title: One semantic action and one handler
requirements.requirement: For every GUI, palette, NL/agent and API action reuse/register a canonical command with typed request/result/error, projected availability/reason, currentness/permissions/FileSafe, one service handler, events/receipts and ObservableWork, forward and reverse wiring, focus/accessibility, idempotency and recovery tests. Shell cmd.panel.switch remains navigation only. Provider-specific legacy cmd.github.* cannot dispatch to a non-GitHub instance because the selected panel changed. Generic adapter-dispatch commands bind explicit provider/resource context. No UI-only direct fetch/mutation handler.
requirements.acceptance: Each action_id maps to exactly one resolved command and handler or documented view-only operation; aliases have schema/payload migration and no ambiguous dispatch.

requirements.title: Command envelope and durable lineage
