requirements.requirement: Common non-secret context includes operation/request ID, actor/Client, Home Server, Project, repository/source location/checkout/host/environment where applicable, instance/connection/profile, expected revision/capability revision, idempotency key and optional Goal/Plan/thread refs. Host-owned mutation revalidates context and acquires leases. External effects have accepted/running/outcome_unknown/observed_complete/failed/partial/cancelled receipts. Read-only commands return observed revision/freshness; they cannot claim fresh state from stale cache. Secure key/code submission uses separate typed secret channels.
requirements.acceptance: JSON schemas and samples distinguish normal operation data and secret material; timeout reconciliation and wrong-instance mismatches have typed errors and tests.

requirements.title: Navigation and UI migration contracts
requirements.requirement: Define typed route targets for source_control repository/change/operation/review, repository_automation service/run/job/log/artifact, Data Backup and Retention destination/snapshot/recovery/restore, and existing Remote Access. Migrate github_actions saved panel routes/bookmarks/shortcuts to the same neutral occupant without changing provider-specific operation identity. Preserve reverse mapping from receipt/error to relevant object and original GUI origin; prevent return-to-wrong-Project after auth. Inputs are stable IDs, never URL interpolation with raw credentials.
requirements.acceptance: Legacy routes/keyboard/panel state deserialize into valid new routes and correct provider; expired object links display explanation rather than silently select another repository.

requirements.title: Secret-action and destructive-action tiers
requirements.requirement: Reading authorized decrypted backup files, exporting a recovery key, revoking a credential and deleting remote backups have different permission scopes. Key export/copy/print and auth secrets are human-only step-up actions, never automatically exposed to model tools. Destructive restore/prune/repository-delete/force-push operations have exact preview hashes, target revisions, confirmation and lease IDs; stale previews are invalid. Silent no-persist is allowed only when a typed receipt explicitly states the reason and contains no sensitive payload.
requirements.acceptance: Policy tests attempt every sensitive action via GUI, API, automation and revoked session; secret output never enters ordinary command/event catalog serialization.

requirements.title: Source and integration DRY owners
requirements.requirement: Use one Repository/Workspace Registry, local VCS adapters/Worktree Manager, RemoteBinding resolver, ForgeAdapter registry, AutomationAdapter registry, capability evaluator, auth/credential brokers and shared projection/cache. Provider-specific payload conversion belongs in adapters, not Settings or panel components. GUI shared components include RepositoryContextHeader, CapabilityAction, RevisionBadge, ReviewRequestList, NativeJobTree, StreamingLogView, ArtifactProvenanceRow and SetupReturnContext. Reuse current equivalents rather than registering synonyms.
requirements.acceptance: Owner/consumer matrix connects every command and UI component; grep plus semantic review finds no shadow provider-specific updater/auth/capability pool.

requirements.title: Backup DRY owners
requirements.requirement: One BackupCoordinator, CaptureBarrierService consumed from storage owners, SourceSnapshotAdapter/GitJJClosureValidator, BackupEngineAdapter, destination registry/transport adapters, scheduler/retention owner, RecoverySetKeyService, SnapshotCatalogProjection and RestoreCoordinator. Secret storage remains shared CredentialBroker, not a backup-only plaintext database. Data Backup and Retention, Bootstrap and Doctor consume these commands/projections. Reusable UI: DestinationCard, ScopeCoverageSummary, SnapshotBrowser, RestorePreview, RecoveryKitHandoff, VerificationBadge, RetentionPreview and ObservableWorkProgress.
requirements.acceptance: Backup, restore, Settings, File Manager and JJ history links resolve to same owner operations; no separate cloud sync or custom crypto subsystem.

requirements.title: Production and reverse wiring evidence
requirements.requirement: For each action record concrete UI source symbol/route, canonical command, request/result/error schema, availability selector, permission rule, sole handler/service, storage family/event/receipt, progress source, deep link, migration alias and test fixture. Reverse wiring starts at handler/event and enumerates every legitimate surface and caller. Keep current Wiring_Matrix.md, production JSON/schema/UI catalogs and automated checks mutually consistent. A command string in Markdown or a demo handler is not wiring proof.
requirements.acceptance: resolved_actions.json joins every packet action to exact live repo evidence; orphan controls, ghost commands and duplicate handlers fail validation.

requirements.title: Plan, schema and generated governance closure
requirements.requirement: Update source-control/Jujutsu/forge/hosted automation owners; backup/restore/storage/retention/credential/auth owners; Tailscale/WAN/deployment/client owners; Settings/FinalGUI/left-rail/Files/Artifacts/Testing/Goal consumers; release supply chain/performance/security/Onboarding/Doctor; commands, schemas, wiring and DRY. Add an owner only after live discovery proves none exists. Preserve PlanUnit/ContractRef/aliases/source lineage and exact-case paths. Regenerate indexes/shards/plan graph/evidence only after canonical edits stabilize; Spec Lock is refreshed at final seal. Do not use stale pipeline/shard/evidence text as canonical product proof.
requirements.acceptance: Per-requirement owner/consumer evidence supports actual semantics; generated bodies are byte-faithful; closure registry avoids recurring unchanged warnings; live repo checks report exact failures, not generic pass.

requirements.title: No reduced fidelity through normalization
requirements.requirement: Machine registries supplement, not replace, detailed prose and required examples. Provider differences, human-key recovery, restart/crash boundaries, type-specific restore and source closure must live in canonical owners near governing rules. Narrow source IDs remain traceable. Defer only true unimplemented external runtime proofs with explicit implementation acceptance gates; do not bury missing contracts under a blanket “capability gated” label. The receiving Goal integrates all supported-provider requirements and transparent unsupported dispositions without claiming feature implementation from plan text.
requirements.acceptance: Independent auditor compares each atomic requirement and provider/panel field to live canonical evidence, not counts or token matches alone.

requirements.title: Minimum end-to-end matrix
requirements.requirement: Cover Git and colocated/non-colocated JJ against every named forge profile, Origin native/mirror, multi-remotes, self-hosted CA, denied scopes and offline hosts; cloud destination families with actual supported auth and encryption; fresh-install loss recovery including historical JJ operations; optional WSL-off Origin platform gap; native/web/standalone/container entry paths; tsnet private/Funnel/Headscale listener and egress behavior. Synthetic contracts may be validated without real accounts, but production integration acceptance requires authorized test accounts/services and exact recorded versions.
requirements.acceptance: Scenarios distinguish specification evidence, mock/fixture contract tests and real integration outcomes. No fixture success becomes provider certification.

requirements.title: Adversarial and concurrency proof
requirements.requirement: Test credential/ref/key leakage, auth callback replay/account mismatch, SSRF/private-metadata redirects, restore archive traversal/reparse/symlink hazards, external source mutations during capture, shared JJ object closure and GC, unknown external publication outcomes, multi-client duplicates, concurrent prune/backup/restore, object deletion/corruption/rollback, lost recovery keys, kit import hostility, Project/Server/connector identity collisions and stale commands after account/Project switch.
requirements.acceptance: Each security scenario has expected fail-closed or partial/recovery behavior and specific evidence; no real user secrets in fixtures.

requirements.title: Performance and GUI proof
requirements.requirement: Measure lazy left-panel hydrate, many repos/accounts/destinations, large graph/snapshot trees, slow logs, 429/poor WAN and multiple clients under active Goals. Respect existing ResourceGovernor limits instead of new magic fixed performance numbers. Verify first interaction never waits for all providers/backup destinations. Test current selected themes, panel widths, undock/reorder/More/keyboard, dialogs and actual motion/reduced-motion states. Record tool capability limits and NOT_RUN status for missing native or visual test environments.
requirements.acceptance: Admitted benchmarks retain interactive reserve; final report includes observed timings/resources and untested claims, not merely screenshots or static syntax.

requirements.title: Preflight and bounded plan
requirements.requirement: Record actual repo revision/status, protected/unrelated user changes, current chosen concept sources/generators, relevant owner docs, command IDs/aliases, active ledgers and prior semantic closures. Read all packet requirements and preserved tsnet prose; create one bounded dependency-aware plan and wait for platform acceptance once, then continue under the same Goal. Use available read-only specialist reviewers for source/forge/UI, backup/security/recovery, tsnet/deployment and cross-owner fidelity; parent is sole canonical writer. A missing named reviewer role is not a reason to fabricate evidence or stall ordinary owner adjudication.
requirements.acceptance: Preflight includes exact baseline and resolved owner/action map; no live write before plan acceptance or unsupported claims that a reviewer was used.

requirements.title: Lossless integration order
requirements.requirement: First resolve shared identities/capabilities/auth/backup key models; then local/forge/CI contracts and adapters; then backup capture/destinations/recovery; then Go connector replacement and shared security boundaries; then commands/schema/wiring/DRY and selected GUI consumers together. Preserve existing GitHub sections via before/after census before generalizing panel. Run narrow validators and semantic review per tranche; checkpoint durable progress. Never overwrite new live files with old packet snapshots or create placeholders to make coverage counts pass.
requirements.acceptance: Every tranche has exact changed files, row-level semantic evidence, validator output and safe resume cursor; existing newer work not in scope remains unchanged.

requirements.title: Closure and final independent audit
requirements.requirement: Every requirement including TSN-001..020 ends with implemented-in-canon, already_canonical, explicitly_superseded-by-row or blocked-with-exact-reason and live evidence. Required product behavior cannot be silently deferred to finish. Distinguish missing runtime test infrastructure from incomplete specification. Resolve aliases/migrations and rehearse validators for side effects; seal governance after canon stable. Independent audit is read-only to product canon and yields bounded repair worklist, not another full rewrite. Reopen prior closures only when evidence/requirements changed.
requirements.acceptance: Final closure joins requirement→PlanUnit/prose→consumer→schema→command→wiring→GUI→test contract, with actual runtime test statuses separate.

requirements.title: Repository configuration versus exact history
requirements.requirement: Full object/operation-history preservation does not authorize copying runtime credentials embedded in mutable .git/config, .jj configuration, credential files, HTTP extraHeaders or URL user-info into the normal backup configuration layer. Extract non-secret remote/settings metadata and record removed credential-bearing fields and required reconnect steps; preserve object/history content exactly, subject to the historical-secret warning. Do not restore executable hooks, external diff/filter/credential-helper commands or unsafe includes as active configuration without explicit trust review. A source-history backup can be exact for commits/operations while intentionally sanitizing activation configuration; disclose that distinction.
requirements.acceptance: Fixture includes credential-bearing remote URL/helper/header and malicious hook; normal restore preserves commit/JJ history but neither leaks credentials nor executes restored config.

requirements.title: Draft connection setup and activation
requirements.requirement: Forge/automation/cloud setup first creates a typed inactive ConnectionDraft with provider/instance/target intent and return context, then starts the shared AuthSession, selects permitted repository or storage path, verifies minimum non-destructive capabilities and activates the connection. It does not need a preexisting fully authenticated Connection to begin. Cancellation expires callbacks and removes only uncommitted draft attachments after safe cleanup, preserving user-owned existing profiles. Connection edit/remove/test/details use shared lifecycle commands; removing a backup connection is never deleting backup data.
requirements.acceptance: First-time no-profile setup has a complete command path, including cancel/restart and atomic activation without global provider configuration changes.

requirements.title: Hosted administration section closure
requirements.requirement: For existing or newly exposed service admin sections, enumerate read and write actions independently: repository/branch policy, CI environments/deployment approvals, secrets and variables, runner list/registration/removal and release assets. Use adapter-generated versioned field schemas, not a lowest-common-denominator form that silently loses provider policy. Preserve existing GitHub admin capabilities. If a corresponding API is unsupported/unimplemented, a clearly labeled external link is valid; a fake successful PM mutation is not. Secret values are submitted through the human-only broker and cannot be read back merely because metadata lists their names. Runner registration requires an explicit execution-host target and consent; it never happens just by enabling CI integration.
requirements.acceptance: Every exposed admin control resolves to command/schema/permissions/receipt or explicit external-only navigation; no unidentified current live section is dropped.

requirements.title: Unsnapshotted changes and editor buffers
requirements.requirement: Record both the captured current filesystem image and the latest preserved Git/JJ repository operation state; these can differ when working files have not been snapshotted into JJ yet. A backup must not silently manufacture new commits/operations merely to make them match. Restore the actual captured dirty working files along with coherent repository metadata and disclose their relationship. Durable PM unsaved editor-buffer recovery records follow their existing Project storage owner; unsaved process-only memory that was never persisted cannot be claimed backed up. The scope report distinguishes saved files, durable recoverable buffers and unavailable transient state.
requirements.acceptance: Restore a JJ workspace with modifications after its latest operation and a PM durable unsaved buffer; preserve history, files and buffer distinctly without forced publication or new hidden source operation.

requirements.title: Where new state is stored
requirements.requirement: Server Catalog owns destination/connection metadata, scheduler occurrences/writer assignments, RecoverySet public metadata and credential references, and cross-Project full-capture indexes. Actual secrets remain in the shared protected credential/key store. Project Vault owns Project-specific concrete source/backup preferences, capture/source lineage, snapshot/restore receipts and relevant source-control/forge binding metadata. Remote engine repositories store encrypted recovery content, not writable PM Project state. Derived snapshot/tree/provider projections are rebuildable. A server-wide backup plan selecting several Projects is an explicit server operational policy, not a general inherited Project-settings layer. Copying Project preferences does not silently transfer cloud credentials, activate duplicate jobs or authorize extra billing. Rebind any moved Project schedule/destination through destination preflight and one-writer transfer.
requirements.acceptance: Storage family registry covers every new record, secret reference and rebuildable projection; project copy/move/full restore retains concrete policy without live scheduler/key duplication.
